+//! The `sodick-ln2w.cps` script suite (#4045, the per-script-suite law of
+//! #926): the post binary on every recorded edge-case stream
+//! (`recorded/streams/*.cnc`), its program or its named refusal compared
+//! with the golden in `recorded/golden/sodick-ln2w/`. The recorded
+//! streams are cutting streams posted machine-less (or on a mill), so the
+//! Sodick LN2W wire post refuses each by name - it posts only wire EDM work on
+//! a machine declared `wire_edm`; its wire program is pinned by app's
+//! `sodick_aq600l`.
+//!
+//! Regenerate after an intentional change, then read the diff:
+//! `WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_sodick_ln2w`
+//!
+//! Gate map (M4.4): covers assets/posts/sodick-ln2w.cps, camcraft_post::post::engine,
+//! camcraft_post::post::cnc, the post binary.
+
+#[macro_use]
+mod recorded;
+
+post_suite!("sodick-ln2w.cps");
+
+// The post's own words on synthetic wire streams (start order, taper, skims, refusals).
+#[path = "sodick_ln2w/pins.rs"]
+mod pins;

+## #4045 - Sodick wire: an LN2W post dialect and a Sodick AQ600L machine file
+
+**What was decided.**
+
+- A second post script, `assets/posts/sodick-ln2w.cps` ("Sodick Wire EDM
+  (LN2W)"), stands beside the Mark 21 script. The Mark 21 script
+  `sodick-wire.cps` has no change, so its output is byte-identical.
+- Each cut starts in the order that the owner of an AQ600L (LN2W) gave:
+  `G00 X Y U0. V0.` (one line), `Z0.`, `T91`, `T84`, `T94`, the `C` word,
+  then the first `G01`. The owner corrected the first order after his
+  round-2 dry run (PR #4065 comment, 2026-11-25): `U0. V0.` goes on the
+  rapid to the start point, not on a line of its own before the cut. This
+  supersedes the order in the #4045 issue comment. `T84` / `T85` and
+  `T94` / `T89` come from `edm.flushing` and `edm.tank`, as in the Mark 21
+  script.
+- The post writes no `G20` or `G21`. The owner's control alarms on `G21`
+  (`E00170`). Thus the script declares `programUnits = "mm"`, and the
+  engine refuses an inch document by name. A header note says that the
